prompt: In `Callbacks.swift`, why was "the request is on its way" printed second, before the course arrived?

choices.text: `print` is faster than a closure
choices.why: Speed has nothing to do with it; the order comes from when each line runs.

choices.text: `loadCourse` returned at once and called back 200 ms later
choices.why: Right: it only scheduled the closure, so the next line of the program ran first.

choices.text: The semaphore reordered the lines
choices.why: The semaphore only kept the program alive until `signal()`.

choices.text: Swift runs the last line of a top-level file before the others
choices.why: Top-level code runs from the top; the closures ran later because they were called later.

prompt: Which problems of completion handlers does section 02 name? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Each dependent step goes one closure deeper
choices.why: Yes: the order on the page stops being the order in time.

choices.text: A path that forgets to call the closure still compiles
choices.why: Yes: and the caller waits for ever.

choices.text: They do not work on Linux
choices.why: They ran on Linux in section 02, through `Dispatch`.

choices.text: An error has no caller left to be thrown to
choices.why: Yes: so handlers grow an error parameter or a `Result`.

prompt: What happens to `Callbacks.swift` if you delete `finished.wait()`?
hint: What keeps the program alive while the closures wait?

choices.text: Nothing changes
choices.why: The wait is what held the process open for 400 ms.

choices.text: It does not compile: a semaphore must be waited on
choices.why: The compiler does not track semaphores.

choices.text: It prints two lines and exits
choices.why: Right: the top level ends before either closure is called.

choices.text: It prints the four lines in the source's order
choices.why: Without the wait the closures never get to print at all.

prompt: What does `await` mark?

choices.text: A suspension point in the function
choices.why: Right: the function pauses there if it has to wait, and other code runs meanwhile.

choices.text: A call that runs on a new thread in parallel
choices.why: `await` promises no parallelism; the two loads ran one after another.

choices.text: A function whose result is optional
choices.why: Optionals are a `?`; `await` is about time.

choices.text: A call the compiler will run at start-up, before the rest
choices.why: It runs where it is written, in order.

prompt: `func report()` contains `await loadCourse(named: "Swift")`. What does the compiler say?

choices.text: Nothing; `await` makes the call legal anywhere
choices.why: A function that is not `async` cannot pause, so it cannot await.

choices.text: A warning that the call is slow
choices.why: It is an error, and no program is written.

choices.text: That `loadCourse` must be `throws`
choices.why: Nothing here throws.

choices.text: 'async' call in a function that does not support concurrency
choices.why: Right, with a note offering to mark `report` `async`.

prompt: While an `async` function waits at an `await`, the ___ it was running on is free to run other work.
hint: Not the function and not the task.

prompt: What does `Task { … }` return to the code that wrote it?

choices.text: The closure's result, after waiting for it
choices.why: It returns at once, before the work has run.

choices.text: A handle on the work, to await
choices.why: Right: `await task.value` gives the result when it exists.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: It returns a `Task<Success, Failure>`.

choices.text: A thread
choices.why: A task is not a thread; many tasks share few threads.

prompt: `Forgotten.swift` printed "done" and never "saved". Why?
hint: When does a script's process end?

choices.text: The task threw an error nobody caught
choices.why: Nothing threw; `try?` was there and the sleep was not cancelled.

choices.text: `Task.sleep` does not work at the top level
choices.why: It worked in every other program of the lesson.

choices.text: The process ended first
choices.why: Right: nothing awaited the task, and the program ended under it.

choices.text: A task prints only when it is detached
choices.why: Any task may print; this one never reached its `print`.

prompt: A task made with `Task { … }` is not tied to the function that created it. Swift calls it ___.
hint: The opposite of what `async let` makes.

prompt: Three independent loads of 300 ms each are awaited one after another. Roughly how many milliseconds does that take?
The same three loads started with `async let` and awaited together. Roughly how many milliseconds?
A function starts `async let report = loadReport()` and then returns early on an error, without awaiting `report`. What happens to the load?
hint: A child task cannot outlive its scope.

choices.text: It keeps running in the background, like `Forgotten.swift`
choices.why: That is an unstructured task; `async let` makes a child.

choices.text: It is cancelled, and awaited, as the scope ends
choices.why: Right: the scope ends, so its child is cancelled and awaited there.

choices.text: The compiler refuses a scope that does not await every `async let`
choices.why: It compiles; the cleanup is done for you at run time.

choices.text: The program crashes
choices.why: Nothing is wrong enough to crash; the child is cancelled.

prompt: In what order does `for await … in group` hand out the results?

choices.text: The order the tasks were added
choices.why: Statistics was added third and came last.

choices.text: Alphabetical order of the course names
choices.why: SQL came before Kotlin.

choices.text: The order they finish
choices.why: Right: SQL at 150 ms, Swift at 250, Kotlin at 300, Statistics at 500.

choices.text: A random order chosen when the group opens
choices.why: The order is the finishing order, which the delays decided.

prompt: Four loads in one group take 150, 250, 300 and 500 ms. Roughly how many milliseconds does the whole group take?
hint: The children run side by side.

prompt: Why does each child in `Group.swift` return `(course, minutes)` and not only the minutes?
hint: Think of a caller that needs Kotlin's minutes.

choices.text: A task group refuses children that return a plain `Int`
choices.why: `withTaskGroup(of: Int.self)` is legal.

choices.text: The results arrive in finishing order, so position says nothing
choices.why: Right: each answer has to name what it belongs to.

choices.text: Tuples are faster to send between tasks
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: To print the name; the sum would be wrong without it
choices.why: The sum is the same in any order.

prompt: What does `task.cancel()` do to a running task?

choices.text: Stops its thread on the spot
choices.why: Swift never stops a task from outside.

choices.text: Sets a flag that its code is expected to check
choices.why: Right: `Task.sleep` and `checkCancellation` read it; a loop that never does keeps going.

choices.text: Throws an error into it at whatever line it is on
choices.why: Errors appear only where the code checks.

choices.text: Deletes its result
choices.why: A cancelled task still produces a result, or an error.

prompt: In `Cooperate.swift`, the careless loop was cancelled after two courses and still returned 270. Why?

choices.text: The cancel came too late to matter
choices.why: It came after two courses; the careful version stopped there.

choices.text: A task group ignored the request
choices.why: There is no group in that program.

choices.text: `try?` discarded each error
choices.why: Right: every sleep threw at once, and the loop carried on.

choices.text: `Task.sleep` does not check for cancellation
choices.why: It does; that is why it threw at once after the cancel.

prompt: Match each piece of code to what it does about cancellation.

pairs.right: Throws `CancellationError` if the task is cancelled
Ends the wait and lets the code carry on
Throws at that line if cancelled, without waiting
A `Bool` the code reads and decides on

right_distractors: Stops every task in the program

prompt: A task started with `Task { … }` inside another task. The outer task is cancelled. What happens to the inner one?

choices.text: It keeps running
choices.why: Right: it is unstructured, not a child, so the cancellation does not reach it.

choices.text: It is cancelled with its parent, like an `async let`
choices.why: Only child tasks are cancelled with their parent.

choices.text: The outer task cannot be cancelled while it holds another task
choices.why: Any task can be cancelled.

choices.text: Both crash
choices.why: Cancellation is a flag, never a crash.

prompt: A planner loads 20 courses in a task group, and one load fails with an error. Which variant makes the other 19 stop instead of finishing for nothing?

choices.text: `withTaskGroup`, with `try?` inside each child
choices.why: `try?` hides the failure, so nothing cancels the rest.

choices.text: Twenty `async let`s
choices.why: Twenty names do not fit a list known only at run time.

choices.text: `withThrowingTaskGroup` and `for try await`
choices.why: Right: the first error is rethrown and the group cancels the other children.

choices.text: Twenty separate `Task { … }` values cancelled one by one in a loop
choices.why: That works only if you write all of it yourself, which the group already does.
